newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude steadying but prompt overhang persists.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude steadying but prompt overhang persists.

text.p: North Sea Brent spot prices were steady but a persistent overhang of prompt barrels kept buyers relaxed and trade thin, dealers said.

Dated Brent was valued steady at the lower levels, discounted to September paper by around 25 cents a barrel, in line with recent trade. But traders said an overhang of early September barrels, especially Statfjord and Gullfaks, made for a bearish, although short term, undertone.
Premiums to benchmark Dated Brent for Forties cargoes held steady after a Sep 12-14 cargo traded on Tuesday at around dated +27 cents tidied up the front end of this market a little.
Ekofisk premiums were also stable with a cargo for Sep 23 trading at Dated Brent +35 cents.

October Brent paper dipped 20-30 cents in early trade after Tuesday's API report showed a bearish 10.4 million barrel U.S. crude stock build. But it began to recover and stood around $20.00-$20.10 a barrel, just 10 cents off Tuesday's European close at around 1200 GMT.
The Sept/Oct paper spread was assessed steady around +43/46 cents but further forward spreads were a couple of cents softer. Oct/Nov talked +38/40 cents and Nov/Dec +36/389 cents.
Traders said at least three early September Brent cargoes were on offer in addition to fairly lengthy looking, Statfjord and Gullfaks supplies.
CFDs were marked slightly softer to reflect then bearish spot market sentiment. Oct 4-10 contracts traded at Oct Brent +14 cents and next week's dates assessed around Oct +12/17 cents.

With three prompt cargoes of Urals still for sale in the Mediterranean many expected prices to go as low as Dated Brent -$1 a barrel. Further forward sellers still held out for Dated -80 cents and reported some refining interest.
The closure of Novorossiisk due to high winds and swell late on Tuesday would give prompt sellers a breathing space, traders said.
"The prompt is very sloppy and those sellers will be very happy the terminal is closed," one said.

West African markets were quiet. Cabinda traded this week at Dated Brent -65 cents and this level was repeatable, traders said. A U.S. trader was heard offering a September 10-11 cargo at Dated -60 cents but buying interest was slow.
Forcados was assessed steady at Dated Brent +30/35 cents with 2/3 cargoes actively offered.
